extracted.intended_audience: researchers and post-publication reviewers (PubPeer commenters and authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and concern taxonomy for commenting on already‑published research on PubPeer — what issues to flag and how to conduct oneself when posting post-publication critiques. Covers image/data/method/citation concerns and norms for commenters and authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Western-blot duplication / band reuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Western-blot duplication / band reuse within or across figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag when identical or highly similar blot bands appear in different lanes, panels, or figures representing different experiments or conditions. Provide figure/panel references and, where possible, annotated images or links to demonstrate duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopy image reuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Microscopy image reuse — same image used to represent different conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify repeated microscopy images presented as distinct samples/conditions. Cite specific figure numbers and panels; include cropped/zoomed comparisons to show reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate splicing / band cropping
rubrics_metrics.description: Inappropriate splicing / band cropping with no marked boundary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note unmarked joins or cropped gel/blot images that combine lanes from different gels or experiments. Indicate expected boundaries and request original blots or clarification from authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate brightness/contrast adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Inappropriate brightness/contrast adjustments that obscure structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out image manipulations (brightness/contrast) that hide features or create misleading appearance. Provide screenshots or forensic-enhanced versions if available, and request original/raw images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pixel-level duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Pixel-level duplication detectable by image-forensics tools (Forensically, ImageTwin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use image-forensics tools to detect exact or near-exact pixel-level matches. Include tool outputs, hashes, or comparison overlays as evidence when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image rotation, flip, or scaling to disguise reuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Image rotation, flip, or scaling used to disguise reuse of the same image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out manipulations such as rotation/flip/scale that likely re-present the same image as different data. Provide aligned comparisons showing transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical impossibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical impossibilities — variance equal to zero where it should not be, GRIM-fail means, terminal-digit anomalies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag impossible or highly implausible summary statistics (e.g., means inconsistent with reported n, variances of zero). Reference GRIM/GRIM-like tests and terminal-digit analysis where applicable, and show calculations or examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data inconsistencies between text, tables, and figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Data inconsistencies between text, tables, and figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out mismatches in reported numbers across the manuscript (e.g., table values not matching figure axes or textual descriptions). Cite exact locations and propose reconciliations or request raw data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implausible precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Implausible precision — reported values incompatible with the measurement instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note reported numeric precision or significant digits that exceed instrument resolution or sampling scheme. Provide reasoning about instrument limits and request clarification or raw measurement data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outlier patterns suggesting fabrication or selective reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Outlier patterns suggesting fabrication or selective reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify suspicious clustering, repeated patterns, or improbable outlier distributions that may indicate fabrication or p-hacking. Show plots or summary analyses that reveal the pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing data not flagged / disappearing or changing data between versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Missing data not flagged; or disappearing/changing data between manuscript versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document instances where datasets are absent, omitted without explanation, or where numbers change between preprint and published versions. Provide links to versions and note the specific differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-replication of the published findings by independent groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report failed replication attempts by independent groups, cite the replication study, and indicate specific divergences in methods or results that undermine the original claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unspecified randomisation or blinding
rubrics_metrics.description: Unspecified randomisation or blinding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag absence of statements about randomisation/blinding where these would be expected. Ask for protocol details or preregistration records to assess risk of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadequate sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: Inadequate sample size undermining the reported effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out underpowered studies or sample sizes inconsistent with claimed effect sizes. Provide power calculations or references to standards where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrong statistical test
rubrics_metrics.description: Wrong statistical test used for the data type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify inappropriate statistical analyses (e.g., parametric tests on non-normal small-sample data) and suggest correct alternatives or request reanalysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism — text similarity with prior literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite passages with suspicious similarity, link to the earlier source, and provide comparison snippets or similarity-score evidence where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation manipulation — citation cartels, missing relevant prior work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out patterns of inappropriate citation behavior (over-citation of a group, omission of key prior art). Provide references to omitted relevant literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorship disputes — undeclared contributions, ghost authorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag indications of disputed or undeclared authorship/contributions, cite acknowledgements or author statements, and request clarification from authors or editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use only publicly verifiable facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use only publicly verifiable facts (rule formally adopted in 2016).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should be based on evidence visible in the public record (figures, tables, text, version history). Avoid private accusations or unverifiable claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: No allegations of misconduct; describe observations not intent
rubrics_metrics.description: No allegations of misconduct — describe the observation, do not impute intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid asserting fraud or deliberate wrongdoing. Phrase posts to describe what is observed (e.g., ‘the image appears duplicated’) rather than concluding malicious intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: One concern per comment
rubrics_metrics.description: One concern per comment — avoid combining multiple observations into a single post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post individual, focused comments for each discrete issue to allow targeted responses and clearer discussion. The page repeats this guidance to emphasize focused reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite sources / link to specific page, figure, or sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite sources — link to specific page, figure, or sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include precise pointers (DOI/page/figure/panel/paragraph) so readers and authors can verify the claim quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral tone — explanatory not accusatory
rubrics_metrics.description: Neutral tone — explanatory, not accusatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain professional, neutral language to facilitate constructive discussion and reduce defensiveness; focus on evidence and questions rather than blame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity permitted but substantiate claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymity is permitted but commenters are encouraged to substantiate every claim publicly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters may post anonymously, but must still provide verifiable evidence and documentation to support their observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors are notified and given right of reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are notified automatically and given right of reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform's workflow includes notifying listed authors so they can respond; expect authors to be given opportunity to address each point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors encouraged to respond on PubPeer
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to respond on PubPeer rather than ignore concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should engage with comments openly on the platform to clarify, correct, or present counter-evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responses should address each numbered point with supporting documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses should address each numbered point with supporting documentation (raw data, original blots, code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are expected to reply point-by-point and supply raw materials (original blots, datasets, code) to resolve concerns when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: If concerns are correct, issue correction/retraction/notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the commenter's concern is correct, authors should issue a correction, retraction, or notice of concern in the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should coordinate with journals to publish formal corrections or retractions as appropriate once errors or misconduct are established.

rubrics_metrics.name: PubPeer concern taxonomy as de facto post-publication checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: The PubPeer concern taxonomy (image, data, methods, citation/authorship) is now the de facto post-publication review checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many journals have incorporated these elements into pre-publication reviewer forms (image-integrity checks, statistical-plausibility checks). Automated tools (ImageTwin, Proofig) implement parts of this taxonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments are not authoritative judgements of misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: PubPeer comments are not themselves authoritative judgements of misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform statements emphasize that final misconduct determinations are made by journals and institutions; PubPeer documents observations for discovery rather than formal adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors/journals/institutions make final determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors retain right of reply and the journal/institution makes any final misconduct determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat a PubPeer comment as a final verdict; expect institutional processes to follow for formal investigations if warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform avoids editorial gatekeeping to maximise discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: The platform deliberately avoids editorial gatekeeping in order to maximise discovery, accepting that some comments will be ill-founded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PubPeer accepts lower barriers to posting to surface issues broadly; readers should weigh comments' evidence rather than assume all flagged issues indicate wrongdoing.
